newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares dip after records, recovery foreseen.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares dip after records, recovery foreseen.

text.p: Danish share prices closed lower in a quiet, low activity market on Friday ending a stream of seven consecutive trading days of record closing highs, with dealers seeing possible rises again on Monday.

"There was a dearth of activity today on top of all the week's bank results with little to focus on. Things should buck up again with rises on Monday when third biggest BG Bank presents its 1996 result," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index lost 1.23 point to end the day at 157.89 in overall bourse turnover of 1.492 billion crowns.
The KFX March future fell 2.05 point to 156.80 with 714 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Unidanmark and Den Danske Bank, their 1996 results announced earlier in the week, both slipped to close four and eight crowns lower respectively at 354 and 618.
BG Bank, its result due on Monday, finished two up at 310.
With the Phoenix takeover battle unresolved and new bids from Superfos and Norway's Rieber, the Danish contractor's share closed five up at 670.
